chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Barqi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyaba, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Tawaf, so I said, 'Do I speed up to three paces or four? He said: 'Walking between the two walks.'

key_terms.الطَّوَاف: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.مَشْيٌ بَيْنَ الْمَشْيَيْنِ: Walking between the two walks (moderate pace)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended pace for walking during Tawaf according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ideal tempo for Tawaf, prescribing a moderate pace that balances the brisk 'raml' (typically performed by men in the first three circuits) with a slower, more contemplative walk. This guidance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *wasatiyyah* (moderation) in ritual acts, ensuring the pilgrim maintains both physical vigor and spiritual presence without rushing or dragging. The ruling underscores the importance of aligning bodily movement with inner devotion during the circumambulation of the Kaaba.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Barqy, from Abdul Rahman Bin Sayaba who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Tawaaf, so I said, ‘Quickly, or mostly (quickly), or slowly?’ Heasws said:’ Walk between the two walks (moderate pace)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Barqiy from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayabah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the manner of walking during Tawaf around the Ka‘bah as to how fast or how slow should I walk. He (the Imam) replied, ‘Walk moderately in between the two kinds of walking.’” (Fatwa best explains the following chapters).
